explain.say: In 1833 a young poet received a letter: his best friend, Arthur Hallam, had died suddenly in Vienna, aged just twenty-two. Alfred Tennyson spent seventeen years writing short poems of grief, and in 1850 published them as In Memoriam A.H.H. The timeline follows that grief from shock to hope.

explain.say: Look at the shape of each stanza on the board: four short lines, each with four beats, rhymed a, b, b, a. Notice how the last line returns to the first sound, like a mind circling back to the same loss. This is called the In Memoriam stanza. Why might a circling rhyme suit grief?

explain.say: Now the darkest part: doubt. Tennyson had read the new geology, which showed whole species dying out in the rocks. He pictures Nature, red in tooth and claw, careless of every creature. That was nine years before Darwin's Origin of Species. If nature is so cruel, can love survive death?

explain.say: On the left, doubt; on the right, faith. Tennyson does not argue his way out; he feels his way, trusting the heart when reason fails. He even writes that there lives more faith in honest doubt than in half the creeds. Queen Victoria, widowed in 1861, said the poem comforted her. Which side wins for you?

The poem ends with a wedding, his sister's, and hope for a better human future. Its best-known lines say it is better to have loved and lost than never to have loved at all. Lovely work. Challenge: read section seven, where he stands outside Hallam's old house, and notice how bare the words become.

faq.q: Who was In Memoriam written for?
faq.a: Arthur Henry Hallam, Tennyson's closest friend from Cambridge, who was engaged to Tennyson's sister Emily. He died suddenly in Vienna in 1833, aged 22.

faq.q: What does Nature, red in tooth and claw mean?
faq.a: Tennyson pictures nature as violent and careless, killing whole species, as fossils showed. The phrase asks how a loving God fits a world of predators and extinction, and later became a catchphrase for Darwin's ideas.
asks: Red in tooth and claw meaning

faq.q: What is the In Memoriam stanza?
faq.a: A four-line stanza of iambic tetrameter, four beats a line, rhymed a b b a. The enclosed rhyme makes each stanza circle back on itself.

faq.q: Is In Memoriam one poem or many?
faq.a: Both. It is one long elegy made of a prologue, 131 numbered sections and an epilogue, written separately over seventeen years and arranged to follow about three years of grief.
asks: How many sections are in In Memoriam?

faq.q: Why was In Memoriam so popular with Victorians?
faq.a: It voiced their own crisis: grief, and fear that science was undermining faith. It offered hard-won hope rather than easy comfort, and Queen Victoria found solace in it after Prince Albert died.
asks: Why did Queen Victoria like In Memoriam?

facts: In Memoriam A.H.H. was published in 1850, the year Tennyson succeeded Wordsworth as Poet Laureate.
Arthur Hallam died in Vienna in September 1833, aged 22.
The poem has a prologue, 131 sections and an epilogue.
